newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane mixed on import rumors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane mixed on import rumors.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were mixed in late trade on Monday as rumors of propane imports put a damper on values, traders said.
Players said that much of the market was talking of seven cargoes being fixed to arrive into the low-stocked U.S. Gulf Coast market, but so far only two have been confirmed.
The cargoes fixed late week were departing from state Algerian oil company, Sonatrach, and Brazilian company, Petrobras, players said.
Four others were rumored heading for a large petrochemical but it could not be confirmed.
In late trade, spot propane in the Gulf held onto the one cent it lost at midday, remaining between 50.50 cents and 50.75 cents a gallon, traders said.
Conway, Kansas, hub spot material, which fell one cent at midday, dropped another one cent in late trade.
"I think people are finally realizing that we had been too high," said a Midwest player.
Natural gasoline, however, saw some upward pressure from the strong gains on NYMEX November gasoline futures, which ended up 2.71 cents at 66.34 cents a gallon.
Traders also attributed natural gasoline's strength to petrochem interest given the high prices for propane in recent weeks.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
